title: Fire-module SqueezeNet1.1 trunk + FiLM-conditioned single field + D4 symmetry + adaptive-sharpening decode (forced pivot, mobilenet_v3_small banned)
hypothesis: 25 straight reverts since champion (exp-35, 743.07 m) have swept nearly every decode/output family (VQ codebook, GMM, dense per-patch consensus, spatial MoE, retrieve-rerank, factorized axes, coarse-to-fine, coordinate-generated field) and nearly every from-scratch-trunk-plus-objective family (contrastive, reconstruction/canonicalization, five from-scratch backbones, exp-61's 4x-wider from-scratch trunk which failed the deployment gate outright) while leaving champion's exact pretrained trunk (mobilenet_v3_small features[:9], 190k params, 48ch@8x8 GAP) and its two-expert gate untouched or barely touched. The single closest post-champion result in the whole history, exp-42 (846.42 m), is the ONE experiment that changed only the trunk's pretraining objective while leaving champion's full field/decode/gate/C4-ensemble shape completely intact -- jointly with exp-61's own capacity analysis, this points at trunk richness (channel width / feature vocabulary), not decode shape, as the binding constraint every decode-family pivot has failed to move. This round bans champion's exact backbone outright, so instead of falling back to a from-scratch trunk (a family already tried 10+ times and consistently starved at ~130k params, per exp-61's own count), it swaps in a genuinely different pretrained family: SqueezeNet1.1's squeeze-then-expand 'fire module' trunk (torchvision, BSD-3, ImageNet-pretrained), truncated to its first 11 layers -- structurally unlike MobileNetV3's depthwise-separable inverted-residual-plus-SE-plus-hardswish blocks, and critically ~8x wider per spatial position (384ch vs 48ch) at a comparable total trunk parameter count (~336k vs 190k), so the field head finally reads a richer descriptor instead of a wider from-scratch stack no prior experiment could make work. Around that new trunk, every downstream stage is rebuilt rather than carried over: the two-expert gate/blend (an unexamined mixture-of-experts mechanism kept unchanged since exp-12, itself ~570k params of duplicated capacity) is replaced by a single FiLM-conditioned head, so the freed duplication budget pays for the wider trunk's field head instead of a second expert; the C4 rotation ensemble becomes full D4 (rotations plus mirror reflections -- aerial views are genuinely left-right symmetric, unlike the handwriting-style tasks C4/D4 usually get used for, and reflection invariance has never been tried); and the fixed-temperature decode sharpening (DECODE_BETA=3.0 constant since exp-14) becomes a per-example learned function of the raw field's own entropy, so confusable (high-entropy) fields get sharpened harder before commit -- attacking the same lookalike-cell problem exp-35's training-side sampling improved, now also from the decode side.
method: model/model.py: delete the mobilenet_v3_small import, PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH/mnv3s_features8.pt load, dark_logits/gate mixture, and fixed DECODE_BETA. Build the trunk from torchvision.models.squeezenet1_1's features[:11] (stem conv + 4 Fire blocks through the third maxpool, ~336k params, ImageNet-pretrained, BSD-3), loading a new checked-in weights slice model/pretrained/squeezenet1_1_features11.pt (same strict-load convention as the file it replaces). Replace the C4 rotation stack with a D4 stack (4 rotations x mirror flip = 8 exact pixel views). Replace the layout-squeeze+GAP+gated-dual-head with ONE FiLM-conditioned head: a tiny brightness-to-(scale,shift) MLP modulates the trunk's ~7x7x384 feature map per-channel before a slim layout squeeze (1 channel) + GAP(384) feed a single Linear to the 32x32 cell logits. Replace fixed DECODE_BETA with a tiny 2-input MLP (raw field entropy + raw field peak mass, both detached) producing a per-example adaptive beta that scales the logits before the softmax soft-argmax commit; the unsharpened field (beta-independent) is still used for CE training and for the confidence head's shape features, mirroring exp-14's separation of 'well-calibrated field' from 'sharpened commit'. Recompute the confidence head over the new descriptor plus the adaptive beta value itself. model/train.py: no structural changes needed -- keep the trunk submodule named self.features so the existing two-tier LR split (trunk 1e-4 / head 1e-3), the confusability-weighted sampler, and the conf_shift calibration all keep working unmodified; only update the one-line init string logged in train_area()'s info dict to name the new pretrained family. ONNX export / estimate_position contracts, GRID_K=32, TARGET_SIGMA_CELLS, and the overall loss_fn shape (Gaussian-CE + coord L2 + conf BCE) are unchanged.
expected_outcome: If trunk richness (not decode shape) is really the binding constraint, worst-case median error should approach or beat the 743.07 m champion, plausibly landing in the 650-950 m range as the wider 384-channel descriptor gives the field head more to separate lookalike cells with. If instead this lands in the 1000-2500 m range typical of every prior architecture-family pivot regardless of family, that is a decisive negative result: it would mean champion's exact pretrained-weights identity (not just 'having a' pretrained trunk with comparable capacity) is doing most of the work, and no further trunk-family swap is worth trying -- the next pivot should stop touching the trunk/decode axis entirely and interrogate the training-data or relighting axis instead. Downside is bounded: an untrained/near-random field still decodes near the map center regardless of the learned beta's initial value (small logits stay ~uniform under any beta scale), so a null result should land near the historical ~2.3-3.2 km untrained-model floor, not a gate failure -- unlike exp-61, the projected ONNX size (~3.2 MiB, ~808k total params at float32) leaves real headroom under the 4 MiB gate rather than assuming it will fit.
eli5: The model's 'eyes' have been the same borrowed eyes for 35 rounds, and the last 25 experiments all tried rearranging what happens AFTER the eyes without touching them -- none of it worked. This round we're not allowed to reuse those eyes at all, so we swap in a different pretrained set that sees the world through wider, richer 'glances' (8x more detail per glance) instead of trying to build new eyes from scratch, which has failed every single time it's been tried. Everything downstream is rebuilt to match: instead of two separate 'day expert' and 'night expert' sub-brains voting on the answer, there's now one brain that just retunes itself based on how bright the photo is; instead of checking the view from 4 rotated angles, we now also check its mirror image, since aerial photos really do look the same flipped left-right; and instead of always squinting at the guess-map by the same fixed amount before committing to an answer, the model now decides per-photo how hard to squint based on how confusing that particular map looks.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px aerial crop, one of 6 simulated lighting conditions

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: a brand-new pretrained trunk: ImageNet-pretrained SqueezeNet1.1 (torchvision, BSD-3), first 11 layers -- stem conv plus 4 'fire' squeeze-then-expand blocks through the third pooling step -- a completely different building block from the banned MobileNetV3 trunk, ~336k params, ~7x7x384 output (8x more channels per position than before), gently fine-tuned

stages.name: Symmetry ensemble
stages.detail: the crop now travels through the trunk in all 8 exact pixel arrangements of the square's full symmetry group -- the previous 4 rotations, plus their mirror images -- since an aerial view really is left-right symmetric; the 8 resulting readings are averaged

stages.name: Lighting-conditioned field head
stages.detail: the old two-expert 'day head / night head blended by a gate' is gone; one field head reads the crop's own brightness and uses it to directly retune (scale and shift) its own feature map before scoring the map's 1,024 cells -- a single head that adapts to the light instead of two heads voting

stages.name: Decode
stages.detail: the heat map is still sharpened before the model commits to an answer, but how hard it gets sharpened is no longer a fixed amount -- a small learned gauge reads the raw map's own spread (one crisp peak vs. a confusing smear) and picks a stronger or weaker sharpening per photo, then the answer is the balance point of that adaptively sharpened map

stages.name: Confidence
stages.detail: recomputed from the new head's descriptor plus the adaptive sharpening amount itself -- how hard the map needed to be squinted at is itself a clue about how sure the model should be; same 'no fix' abstention idea, same tuned bar and per-bucket floor

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: the map-cell grading and position-error grading keep the same shape as before, but the position-error grading now also teaches the new adaptive-sharpening gauge, since the commit it grades depends on it

implementation_brief:
GENERATE THE WEIGHTS FILE FIRST (one-time, offline): using torchvision, run `from torchvision.models import squeezenet1_1, SqueezeNet1_1_Weights; m = squeezenet1_1(weights=SqueezeNet1_1_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1); sub = m.features[:11]; torch.save(sub.state_dict(), 'model/pretrained/squeezenet1_1_features11.pt')`. Saving the SLICED SUBMODULE's own state_dict (not the full model's) means the keys are already '0.weight', '3.squeeze.weight', etc. with no 'features.' prefix to strip -- load it directly with `trunk.load_state_dict(torch.load(path, map_location='cpu', weights_only=True), strict=True)`, no key manipulation needed (this differs from the mnv3s_features8.pt convention, which saved from the full model and stripped a prefix -- do not copy that stripping step here, it would break the strict load since these keys never had the prefix).

model/model.py: (1) Remove `from torchvision.models import mobilenet_v3_small`, PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH pointing at mnv3s_features8.pt, and `_build_pretrained_trunk`'s mobilenet-specific body; replace with `from torchvision.models import squeezenet1_1` and a `_build_pretrained_trunk()` that builds `squeezenet1_1(weights=None).features[:11]` and loads the new .pt file as above. Keep the trunk assigned to `self.features` in TinyLocNet (train.py's two-tier LR split does `model.features.parameters()` -- keeping this attribute name means train.py needs NO changes for that logic). Keep IMAGENET_MEAN/IMAGENET_STD buffers and the `(x - norm_mean) / norm_std` normalization in forward() exactly as before (still an ImageNet-pretrained trunk). (2) Replace `_c4_stack` with `_d4_stack(x)`: build the existing 4 rotations (identity, transpose+flip r90, flip r180, transpose+flip r270) then also append each of their horizontal mirrors (`.flip(3)`), giving 8 views concatenated on dim 0; keep it pure exact-pixel index ops, no interpolation. (3) Delete `dark_logits` and `gate`; add a `film = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 2 * feat_ch))` built after the dynamic trunk-output probe (same probe pattern already in `__init__` to get feat_ch/fmap_hw). In forward(), compute `film_out = self.film(lum)` (lum = per-crop raw-pixel mean brightness, same rotation-invariant scalar already computed, repeated x8 for the D4 stack), split into `scale, shift = film_out.chunk(2, dim=1)`, apply `fmap_mod = fmap * (1 + torch.tanh(scale)).view(-1, feat_ch, 1, 1) + shift.view(-1, feat_ch, 1, 1)` -- the `1 + tanh(...)` keeps scale near 1 at init (small random weights -> tanh~0) so the modulation starts near-identity. Feed `fmap_mod` (not raw `fmap`) into a `layout_squeeze = nn.Conv2d(feat_ch, 1, 1)` (LAYOUT_CH=1, deliberately narrow since GAP is now 384-d, not 48-d -- this keeps the field head's total input width, and thus its Linear-layer byte cost, in the same ballpark as champion's ~570k-param head) and into GAP; concatenate flattened layout code + GAP into one `loc_logits = nn.Linear(feat_ch + fmap_hw*fmap_hw, GRID_K*GRID_K)`; average its 8-view output exactly like champion averaged its 4-view logits. (4) Add `beta_mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 1))`. In forward(), after computing raw `p1 = softmax(logits, dim=1)` (unsharpened, 8-view-averaged), compute detached stats `peak_raw = p1.detach().max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values` and `ent_raw = -(p1.detach() * torch.log(p1.detach() + 1e-9)).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True) / log(GRID_K*GRID_K)`; `beta = 1.0 + F.softplus(self.beta_mlp(torch.cat([ent_raw, peak_raw], dim=1)))`; `p_adapt = softmax(beta * logits, dim=1)`; decode `(u, v)` from `p_adapt` (this is what flies and what coord_loss trains against -- replaces the old fixed-DECODE_BETA softmax). Keep `(u1, v1)` from `p1` only for the confidence head's gap feature, exactly like champion's exp-14 split. (5) Confidence head: `conf_head = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(feat_ch + 4, 32), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(32, 1))` reading `[f.detach() (384-d averaged GAP across the 8 views), peak_adapt, ent_raw, beta.detach(), gap]` where `peak_adapt = p_adapt.detach().max(...)`, `gap = sqrt((u-u1)**2+(v-v1)**2+eps)` all detached exactly like champion -- keep `conf_shift` buffer and the `sigmoid(z - conf_shift)` output unchanged so train.py's `calibrate_conf_shift` needs zero changes. (6) `loss_fn` keeps its exact current shape (CE of raw `logits` against the Gaussian-smoothed target at temperature 1, `coord_loss` on `pred[:, :2]`, `conf_loss` BCE) -- no code change needed there since it already reads `pred`/`logits` generically; the new beta_mlp gets its gradient purely by being in the `pred[:, :2]` computation graph. (7) `export_onnx` and `estimate_position` are untouched -- ONNX input/output contract (1x3x128x128 float32 in, [[u,v,conf]] out) is preserved.

model/train.py: the ONLY required edit is the `info['init']` string in `train_area()` (~line 283) -- change it to `'pretrained:squeezenet1_1 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..10] (torchvision, BSD-3)'`. Everything else (compute_cell_weights confusability sampling, sample_epoch, prepare_realizations, calibrate_conf_shift, the trunk/head LR split, EPOCH_MULT/cosine schedule) is untouched and must keep working against the new model unmodified -- if `model.features.parameters()` or `model(xb)`/`model(xb, return_logits=True)` call shapes don't match, that's a bug in the model.py edit, not something to patch around in train.py.

Before declaring done: verify strict state_dict load succeeds, `export_onnx` runs and the resulting file is comfortably under 4 MiB (projected ~3.2 MiB), and that an untrained (freshly initialized, unloaded-pretrained-only) forward pass still decodes near the map center for a few random crops -- the bounded-downside sanity check every kept experiment since exp-14 has preserved.
